Build one arm per row of a grid of settings

Source: R/core-bench-sweep.R
hr_sweep.Rd

hr_sweep() turns a grid of settings into arms for hr_benchmark(), one per row, each named after its settings and recording them, so the benchmark gets a param.<name> column per setting and a sweep is summarised with aggregate() or hr_report() like any other comparison.

Usage

hr_sweep(base, grid, name = NULL)

Arguments

base

A function of the grid's columns that returns an hr_arm(), an arm made by gr_arm(), or a chain made by hr_chain().

grid

A data frame with one row per arm and one column per setting, or a named list of values, which is crossed with expand.grid(). A setting whose values are not single values (an effort map, a vector of cleaners) goes in a list column, for instance with I().

name

NULL to name each arm after the base arm's name and its settings, as "needle:top_k=2,max_tokens=200"; one string to use in place of the base arm's name; or one string per row.

Value

A list of hr_arm() objects named by arm, one per distinct row, each with its row's settings recorded.

Details

base is either a function or an arm:

A function

Called once per row with the row's values as named arguments, and must return an hr_arm(). A column it has no argument for (and no ... to take) is an error.

An arm made by gr_arm()

Each row's values replace the arm's settings of the same name, and the arm is built again with gr_arm(). A column may be any setting answer_document() takes as an override (see gr_settings_table()), or recipe. A name that is none of these is an error that lists the names that are.

A chain made by hr_chain()

Each column is a setting's path, "step.setting", as hr_settings() lists them, and the chain is built again with the row's values by hr_set(): hr_sweep(chain, data.frame(retrieve.top_k = c(2, 8))). A path that is not a setting of a step's schema is an error that lists the paths that are.

An arm made by hr_arm() alone records no settings, so it cannot be swept by name; give a function that builds it instead.

Rows that build the same configuration are collapsed: the first is kept and the others are dropped with a message of class hr_sweep_collapsed naming them. Two arms from gr_arm() have the same configuration when their recipes resolve to the same settings, so a row that sets a setting to the recipe's own value is the base arm again. Any other two arms have the same configuration when everything but their names is the same, including the values their code reads and the values read by any helper function it calls by name: a function that ignores one of its arguments builds the same arm for every value of it. A value held in an environment rather than read by name is not compared, and neither is a helper reached through a list or another object (h$ask()), whose code is compared but not the values it reads. Two such arms can look like one configuration here and still send different requests, and a sweep would keep only one of them: call such helpers by name, or check with hr_sweep_check(), which compares what was sent.

Sweeping one setting at a time on the dev split, then comparing the arm chosen with the default on test, is the order vignette("compare") follows. hr_sweep_check() then says which settings changed nothing that was sent.

See also

hr_benchmark(), hr_sweep_check(), gr_arm(), hr_chain(), hr_set(), gr_settings_table(), vignette("compare")

Examples

# Sweep a recipe's settings by name.
arms <- hr_sweep(gr_arm("needle"), list(top_k = c(2, 4, 8)))
names(arms)
#> [1] "needle:top_k=2" "needle:top_k=4" "needle:top_k=8"

# The same with a function, crossing two settings.
arms <- hr_sweep(function(top_k, max_tokens) {
  gr_arm("needle", list(top_k = top_k, max_tokens = max_tokens))
}, expand.grid(top_k = c(2, 8), max_tokens = c(200, 500)))
names(arms)
#> [1] "needle:top_k=2,max_tokens=200" "needle:top_k=8,max_tokens=200"
#> [3] "needle:top_k=2,max_tokens=500" "needle:top_k=8,max_tokens=500"

cl <- hr_mock_client(function(m, p) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")
ref <- gr_qa_reference(
  questions = c(revenue = "What was revenue in 2024?"),
  documents = gr_example(), answers = list("45.2 million"), split = "test")
old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE, embedder = "lexical")
bench <- hr_benchmark(arms, ref, runs = 5, client = cl,
                      scorer = gr_scorer_answer())
aggregate(correct ~ param.top_k + param.max_tokens, bench, mean)
#>   param.top_k param.max_tokens correct
#> 1           2              200       1
#> 2           8              200       1
#> 3           2              500       1
#> 4           8              500       1
hr_options(old)
